summary: This defines the Song class, the building block for the playlist we will build throughout the chapter. Each Song object carries a title, artist, genre, and energy level, and knows how to describe itself as a line of text.

lines.text: Energy level is stored as an int rather than text so it can be compared numerically later, which is exactly what a PriorityQueue needs to decide which song plays next.

lines.text: The constructor demands all four values up front, so there is no way to create a half-filled Song floating around your playlist.
The parameter and the field share the name title, so `this.title` is how you say "the field belonging to this object" instead of the value that was just passed in.
The fields are private and only these getters read them back, so once a Song is created its details cannot be quietly changed from elsewhere in the program.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method inherited from Object; if you misspell the method name, you get an error instead of a method that is silently never called.
Because toString is overridden, printing a Song or a whole collection of Songs produces readable lines rather than cryptic object addresses.
